title: Arrested (Acts 21–22)
hookLine: a riot in the Temple and Paul tells his own story

lines: TO THE TEMPLE, TO KEEP A VOW.
cards: Paul reaches Jerusalem. Friends along the way had begged him not to go. A prophet named Agabus even tied his own hands and feet with Paul's belt to show what was coming.

Paul went anyway. In Jerusalem, James and the elders welcome him, and to show he still honors the Law, Paul goes to the Temple to be purified with four men under a vow. He's a Jew, worshiping in the Temple of his people.
And that's where it all breaks loose.

teach.b: Some visitors from Asia see Paul in the Temple and shout that he has brought Greeks into the holy place. He hadn't. They'd seen him in the city earlier with Trophimus, a Gentile from Ephesus, and assumed.
The crowd seizes Paul, drags him out, and the gates are shut. They're trying to kill him when word reaches the Roman commander of the garrison, who runs down with soldiers. The beating stops.
Paul is chained and carried up the steps of the barracks, the crowd is so violent.

teach.h: A JEW OF TARSUS, ASKING TO SPEAK.
teach.b: At the top of the steps, bruised and in chains, Paul asks to speak. The commander is surprised he speaks Greek. Paul says he is a Jew of Tarsus in Cilicia, in the Douay-Rheims, "a citizen of no mean city."
Then he turns and speaks to the crowd in their own language, Hebrew or Aramaic, and they fall quiet. What does he say? Not an argument.
His story. I was brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel. I persecuted this Way.

teach.h: SAUL, SAUL, WHY PERSECUTEST THOU ME?
teach.b: On the road to Damascus a light shone around me, and I heard a voice: "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?" Then a devout man named Ananias came and said, Brother Saul, look up.
That's all: what happened to him. They listen, until he says the Lord sent him to the Gentiles. Then the uproar starts again.
Later, about to be flogged, Paul quietly asks the centurion whether it's lawful to scourge a Roman citizen who hasn't been condemned. It isn't. The flogging stops.

how: In Catholic parishes, adults entering the Church often share their faith story with sponsors and the community during their preparation, and Catholics speak of giving witness by telling plainly what God has done in their lives.

games.q: you're Paul, chained, bruised, carried up the barracks steps away from a furious crowd. what do you do?
o: stay quiet and let the soldiers take you in.
ask to speak to the crowd, and tell them your story.
demand your rights as a Roman at once.
games.why: he asks to speak, the crowd falls silent, and he tells them in their own language what happened to him. he mentions his citizenship only later, when they're about to flog him.

practice: If someone asked why you're on this path, practicing, listening, whatever brought you here, what would you say?

Not an argument, just what happened: who you were before, one moment that changed something, where you are now, in three short sentences in your head. It doesn't have to be dramatic, and if you pray, thank God for one moment in it.

wordCard.voice: Arrested. Paul, seized in the Temple over a rumor, rescued by Roman soldiers, and given the steps of a barracks to tell his own story. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: in the Hebrew tongue, how Paul addressed the crowd. scholars think it means Aramaic, the everyday language.

carryVoice: Your line: tell what happened. A quiet story told honestly is still yours. That's day five hundred fifty-five.
